headline: Sterling Corp and Nakamura Financial Confirm Historic Merger, Form Sterling-Nakamura
body: In a joint announcement broadcast simultaneously from New Chicago's provisional Federal Remnant hall and Nakamura Financial's Osaka-Pacific datacenter, Sterling Corporation and Nakamura Financial confirmed the completion of their 340-billion-phi merger, creating the entity now designated Sterling-Nakamura. The deal — eighteen months in negotiation and widely anticipated since the dollar's collapse earlier this year — unites Sterling's legacy infrastructure financing portfolio with Nakamura's dominant position in algorithmic currency markets, giving the new corponation unparalleled influence over Meridian 88's emerging financial architecture. CEO Elara Voss-Nakamura, granddaughter of Nakamura Financial's founder and the merger's principal architect, called it 'not a consolidation but a convergence — the foundation of something that will outlast every government that has ever failed this region.' The Federal Remnant's Commerce Office confirmed Sterling-Nakamura's provisional sovereignty charter within hours, a speed that critics called 'suspiciously rehearsed.'
aftermath: Sterling-Nakamura's early monopoly on construction financing gave it decisive leverage over which districts of Meridian 88 received development priority, shaping the city's inequality architecture for the next century.
runner_relevance: The merger announcement triggered a wave of corporate intelligence contracts as rival corponations scrambled to understand Sterling-Nakamura's consolidated asset holdings and loan leverage positions. Runners were hired for data extraction from both legacy Sterling and Nakamura server farms before archival migration could obscure the paper trail. The Graycloaks began their long-running operation to acquire Sterling-Nakamura internal communications, funding courier and infiltration contracts that paid between 3,000 and 15,000 phi depending on classification tier.
